additional_info.subject: 0473279 - ID0473279-DC/Si-D/NO-[Multi] OCPP data overload CRM:00314000259
additional_info.body:
Hello Simen,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0473279.
In this ticket I saw, from past conversation with colleagues, that several problems are mentioned on several chargers: great amount of data sent in the StopTransaction message, BootNotification rejected, OCPP offline,etc. Let's tackle one issue at the time.
I will start with the analysis of the amount of data sent in the StopTransaction message, for which this ticket has been opened:
I checked the logs of Stop Transaction, and I can exactly see that in the StopTransaction message several Energy.Active.Import.Register values are sent.
I checked the OCPP keys in the config file of the charger, and the log line represents what it is configured from the Backend:
According to OCPP 1.6, the configuration key "StopTxnAlignedData" says that "Clock-aligned periodic measurand(s) to be included in the TransactionData element of StopTransaction.req MeterValues.req PDU for every ClockAlignedDataInterval of the Transaction".
This is exactly what it is configured in terms of OCPP configuration keys. In the Stop transaction we send the Energy.Active.Import.Register (as per configured in the StopTxnAlignedData key) at every 5 minutes of the charging session (as per configured in the ClockAlignedDataInterval key).
If the Backend is complaining about the amount of data that we send in the StopTransaction, is because they configured it. I compared the configuration with a charger where this is not set, and you can see the different keys as:
I would start to advise the Backend about this configuration, and then further investigate the other issues once this configuration from Backend is restored. For what concerns then the issues on the BootNotification and/or offline connection, I would kindly ask you to provide me timestamps that I can analyze, once the configuration form Backend has been solved.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon.
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: 0473279 - ID0473279-DC/Si-D/NO-[Multi] OCPP data overload CRM:00314000259
additional_info.body:
Hey Simen,
I am following on case
ID0473279.
The open point from the end customer was to get an explanation why, on 2026.01.14T09:53 they received a huge amount of OCPP logs on charger
17000222.
I checked the logs, and found the issue:
A reboot was triggered around 09:30
Once the charger booted up, in a time frame of 10-20 minutes the charger spammed the logs by reporting a huge amount of logs from previous weeks.
At the time, the charger was on FW v8.0.5.
This was an old issue identified on FW v7 and v8, which back in the days it was fixed by Hotfix called "FileHandler".
This Hotfix is included in v8.1.4, and the charger is now currently running on v8.1.4.
For this topic, there is no further issue as the amount of data happened due to an old issue which is now fixed.
You can report this to the customer, and waiting for a feedback from their side in regards of the Energy.Active:import.Register frequency sent in the StopTransaction message.
Looking forward to hearing feedback form you!
